title: One book, two books: plurals (Singular und Plural)
summary: German has several plural endings, but the plural article is always die. Learn the main patterns and count things.
goals: Count things: zwei Stühle, drei Bücher

sections.title: The good news and the bad news
sections.text:
The good news: in the plural the article is **always die**, whatever the gender: [[der Tisch]] - [[die Tische]], [[das Buch]] - [[die Bücher]], [[die Lampe]] - [[die Lampen]].

The bad news: there are several plural endings, and mostly you learn the plural together with each noun, like the article. Your word cards show every plural.

[[ein]] has no plural: [[ein Buch]], but just [[Bücher]] ([[Ich habe Bücher.]]). [[kein]] has one: [[keine Bücher]].

sections.title: The main plural patterns
rows: no ending, sometimes an umlaut (der/das words in -er, -el, -en)

sections.text: Two quick rules that are almost always right: feminine nouns ending in **-e** add **-n** ([[die Tasche]] - [[die Taschen]]), and English words add **-s** ([[das Handy]] - [[die Handys]]), except words in -er: [[der Computer]] - [[die Computer]].

After a number, German uses the plural: [[zwei Bücher]], [[fünf Bücher]] (except measures and money: [[zwei Kaffee]], [[zehn Euro]]). Armenian keeps the singular after numbers (երկու գիրք), and Russian changes the form with the number (два стула, пять стульев). German has neither complication: number + plural.
A plural subject needs the plural verb: [[Der Stuhl ist neu.]] but [[Die Stühle sind neu.]]

items.de: Die Kinder sind drei und fünf.
items.en: The children are three and five.

sections.title: Listen and repeat: singular and plural

items.explanation: der Stuhl, die Stühle: -e with an umlaut.
Plural subject, plural verb: die Bücher sind.

items.question: Which article do all plurals use?
items.explanation: Every plural takes die: die Tische, die Bücher, die Lampen.
